skill: Select the offered set of entries to replace by zero so the resulting ordinary matrix is in row echelon form.
learner_operation: For each offered coordinate set, mentally zero exactly those entries, locate each remaining row leading entry, check strictly increasing leading columns and bottom-only zero rows; select the unique successful offered operation.
reasoning_steps: Identify row-leading nonzero positions and zero rows.
Apply each candidate replacement set, recomputing leading positions or newly zero rows.
Reject equal/decreasing leading columns and internal zero rows.
Choose the offered set producing row echelon form and explain the transformed matrix.
response_contract: All 15 source practice questions use one radio field with five coordinate-set choices, exactly one correct. Canonical example supplies a solution but no answer bank. Multiple mathematically possible operations outside the bank are allowed; do not infer globally unique or minimal replacement sets.
difficulty: moderate; 4 by 4 ordinary integer matrices, coordinate sets usually two or three, no row arithmetic required.
invariants: Only entry replacement by zero; no Gaussian elimination or row swaps.
Row echelon means zero rows at bottom and strictly rightward leading entries; unit pivots are not required.
A single correct offered operation; every offered distractor must fail the actual row-echelon test.
Prompt, coordinate bank, transformed matrix and solution must depend on the same instance.
permitted_variations: Nonzero magnitudes and signs are irrelevant to echelon status and may vary.
Zero/nonzero structure, pivot destinations, preexisting/became-zero rows and specific correct coordinates may vary within the same 4 by 4 workload.
Eligible correct sets, offered distractor profiles, and option positions should vary; original masks and source-specific correct coordinates are incidental assignments, not definitions of the skill.
answer_roles: Coordinates being removed versus retained leading entries can change when zero structure changes.
Two- and three-entry successful operations occur in source; no instructional basis fixes count by recognizable source mask.
The correct radio position is incidental.

source_passages.quote: All the zero rows (rows with only zeros), if any, are placed at the bottom of the matrix; Each leading entry of a row is in a column to the right of the leading entry of the row above it.
The first non-zero entry on each row (from left to right) is called the leading entry of that row.

source_passages.observation: Correct offered set a21,a43; all other offered operations fail.
Preexisting bottom zero row; correct a22,a32,a33 shifts successive leading columns.
Correct a22,a33,a44 creates two bottom zero rows; do not require preserving all pivots.
